title: "Practical_2_Data_Frames_and_Plots/worked_example.qmd"

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)

#I have read the csv file and viewed it in R
bird_breeding_sites <- read_csv("data/breeding_site_locations.csv")
gt(bird_breeding_sites)

#Use colnames to view just column names
colnames(bird_breeding_sites)

#Use glimpse to see a summary of the table
glimpse(bird_breeding_sites)

#<chr> or <dbl> refers to character or numeric data in the column

#nrow or ncol can be used to see number of rows or columns. dim can be used to see both the dimensions

print(ncol(bird_breeding_sites))
print(nrow(bird_breeding_sites))
print(dim(bird_breeding_sites))

bird_migration_sites <- read_csv("data/migratory_connectivity_dataset.csv")

#only want to see first 10 rows so use head function

gt(head(bird_migration_sites))
glimpse(bird_migration_sites)

#100 rows and 34 columns. Tag is CHR and Birth is DBL

bird_breeding_useful <- bird_breeding_sites |> select(Site, Longitude, Latitude) |> distinct() |> rename(Breeding_Longitude = Longitude, Breeding_Latitude = Latitude)

gt(bird_breeding_useful) 

#distinct ensures that no duplicate rows are selected and rename makes column names more clear

#Do same for bird migration sites

bird_migration_useful <- bird_migration_sites |> select(Site, winterLongitude, winterLatitude, pslon, pslat, iblon, iblat, awestlon, awestlat) |> distinct() |> rename(Winter_Longitude = winterLongitude, Winter_Latitude = winterLatitude, Stopover_Longitude = pslon, Stopover_Latitude = pslat, Iberian_Latitude = iblat, Iberian_Longitute = iblon, Westmost_Longitude = awestlon, Westmost_Latitude = awestlat)
gt(bird_migration_useful)

#I will exclude spain from bird breeding and migration

bird_breeding_notspain <- bird_breeding_useful |> filter(Site != "Spain")
bird_migration_notspain <- bird_migration_useful |> filter(Site != "Spain")
gt(bird_migration_notspain)
gt(bird_breeding_notspain)

```
